decision: MVP is the TypeScript client; MCP and agent kit come later
why: user said ts client is the important mvp part and agent things are not priority

decision: measured spec drift 6.1.3-r1 to 7.0.1-r1 before deciding version architecture
why: user questioned per-version entrypoints from research.md; wanted facts before picking
evidence: scratchpad/tools/diff.mjs output: 1 op added, 3 schemas with additive fields, 2 ops doc-only

decision: monorepo via vp create vite:monorepo, sdk via vp create vite:library in packages/sdk, removed sample app and utils
why: user asked for monorepo with libraries under packages using vp cli
result: vp check, vp test, vp pack green

decision: fixed template dts option from tsgo:true to generator:tsgo
why: vp pack crashed with Cannot create property path on boolean true from the in-monorepo template

decision: package name redmine-ts-sdk
why: matches research.md and is free on npm (E404)

decision: vendored spec tags 6.1.3-r1 and 7.0.1-r1 under spec/ with fetch.sh
why: spec author advises pinning exact tags; builds must not need network

decision: ran architect/arena with three runners: Opus free, Sonnet free, Opus steelmanning research.md per-version subpaths
why: version strategy is contested by the user and is the costliest decision after publish; a steelman runner makes sure the research design gets a fair hearing

decision: delegated Docker Redmine 7.0/6.1 harness to a Sonnet worker in its own worktree, in parallel with design
why: verification harness comes before features and is independent of the design; riskiest unknown is seeding a real Redmine non-interactively

decision: workers on Opus and Sonnet via T3; cross-family models only for read-only judging and trail review
why: user asked for opus or sonnet subagents; the review skills want a different model family to catch same-family blind spots

decision: accepted Docker harness: redmine 7.0, 6.1, and 7.0 under /redmine subpath via a 5-line config.ru map; idempotent Ruby seed
why: reviewed the diff and reran up plus smoke from main rather than trusting the worker report

decision: after the running GPT judge finishes, use only Anthropic Claude models for every worker and reviewer, including the final trail review
why: user directive mid-session

decision: chose one superset entrypoint with an optional declared version over per-version subpaths
why: 6.1.3 to 7.0.1 adds one op and four fields; A and B converged on it independently and the steelman runner C conceded it is simpler at this drift

decision: public surface from A (one flat-object input per method, no public ops or rm.call), internals from B (pure wire, engine without generated imports, Listing errors, Extras no-shadow check)
why: cross-judge scored A 22, C 21, B 20 citing B's overlapping entry points and public descriptors; object args are also the TypeScript guidance
result: judge and I disagreed on base, resolved by grafting

decision: dropped A's DELETE-404-on-retry-equals-success rule
why: judge showed removeUsersFromGroup returns 404 legitimately, so a 404 on retry proves nothing

decision: requiredness rule: required only if latest spec requires it and the property exists in every supported version
why: keeps journal fields required (spec precision) while making is_for_all optional (absent in 6.1)

decision: isolatedDeclarations on for the sdk; generated code must annotate exported consts
why: vp check does not enforce it but vp pack (tsgo dts) does; explicit public types suit a library

decision: src typechecks without node types (lib dom, types empty); tests get node types via tests/tsconfig.json
why: research requires no node: imports; a probe file using process.env failed vp check as intended

decision: Fable reserved for the hardest steps; Opus and Sonnet are the default workers
why: user directive: fable is much stronger, use only when needed

decision: launched generator (Opus, worktree) and core runtime (Sonnet, worktree) in parallel against the committed contract
why: the engine never imports generated data, so the two halves only meet at core/op.ts; disjoint write scopes avoid shared state
evidence: commit 730431e, T3 tasks redmine-wave1-generator-r1 and redmine-wave1-core-r1

decision: observed real 6.1 and 7.0: unknown body attributes are ignored (201); superset request types are safe
why: candidate A named this as the superset design's biggest unverified risk

decision: include=relations and include=children omit the key when empty; only journals, allowed_statuses, attachments, watchers, changesets may narrow to required
why: Included<T,I> must not promise a property the server leaves out

decision: undocumented filter operator returns 0 rows, unknown filter key is ignored and returns all rows
why: corrects the design doc claim that both return everything; pre-network rejection still justified

decision: bulk removeUsersFromGroup is 404 on real 6.1 and 204 on 7.0
why: confirms the since 7.0 metadata the version gate depends on, against servers rather than specs

decision: accepted generator after reviewing diff and rerunning gates on main: 94 ops, 8 hidden, 38 schemas, drift as measured
why: own rerun of vp check, tests, pack, gen:check rather than trusting the report

decision: kept the generator's deviations: news.listByProject and search.listByProject stay visible; paged needs total_count, offset and limit
why: global news list has no project_id filter and global search cannot scope to one project, so hiding them would lose capability; the generator now proves any hidden variant's sibling takes the scope key

decision: added overlay.sparseIncludes so include narrowing only promises keys the server always returns
why: probe showed seven include keys absent when their collection is empty
result: type tests fail when the rule is removed, pass with it

decision: accepted core runtime after review: 189 unit tests, worker mutation-checked 36 behaviors, path guard keeps raw requests inside baseUrl
why: reviewed diff and reran gates on main after merging with the generator

decision: switched extras to direct generated op references and fixed ReturnOf<AnyOp> = never
why: registry lookups by id were only needed while generation was a placeholder; ReturnOf matched the input slot against never

decision: ran the built dist against Docker 7.0, 6.1 and 7.0 subpath
why: prove the integrated client on real servers before writing contract tests
result: all checks pass on all three; 6.1 refuses removeUsers locally
